3.speaker: Symon Holl
3.text: “We have to be careful as to what we fund so we have resources remaining for another investment project.”

4.speaker: Symon Holl
4.text: “Today is a big day. We must prioritise our spending wisely in order to achieve the goals we set as a government.”

5.speaker: Symon Holl
5.text: “Agreed, we have to make strategic decisions about our budget since our resources are fairly limited.”

7.speaker: Player
7.text: “Thanks to Symon's expertise, I am sure we will achieve lots of great things today.”

13.speaker: Symon Holl
13.text: “However, under these circumstances, it would worsen the economic crisis if we push it too far. It’s difficult for us to raise debt with the current unhealthy economy, but we can increase the amount of debt we can take as the economy improves.”

14.speaker: Symon Holl
14.text: “As much as we realistically can. If we fail at improving our economy, the promises don't mean much in the big picture.”

15.speaker: Lucian Galade
15.text: “While maintaining enough political support, If I may add. Promises were made during the election.”

16.speaker: Player
16.text: “We should prioritise the most critical branches.”

17.speaker: Lucian Galade
17.text: “One of the reasons our government was elected was because we promised that we are going to focus on the military during our campaign.”

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “Reduction of funding in certain branches can help fund investment projects.”

19.speaker: Symon Holl
19.text: “Yes. The bigger our budget surplus is the more we can spend on reviving the economy.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “We have to keep true to the election promises. Our people voted for us because of the promises we made.”

21.speaker: Nia Morgna
21.text: “Law enforcement is certainly a high priority. However, I feel tackling internal corruption is of far higher importance than increasing our police presence."

22.speaker: Lileas Graf
22.text: “We have so many internal threats to tackle and I'm already stretching my units far too thin with the limited resources allocated to me.”

23.speaker: Lileas Graf
23.text: “I would like to have an increase in the funding of law enforcement to increase the size of the police force and raise salaries.”

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: The preparations for the government budget were finished. Most of the cabinet gathered in the White Room for the important occasion.

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: Nearly half a year had passed since my inauguration. The cabinet looked over-worked.

26.speaker: Player
26.text: “I would like to use this opportunity for a statement.”

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “And now, the moment we've all been waiting for. It's finally time to discuss the government budget.”

29.speaker: Symon Holl
29.text: “I'm quivering in my loafers with excitement, Mr. President.”

33.speaker: Player
33.text: “Six months ago, all of us gathered to change the course of history. Now I'm proud of what we've achieved and what is to come.”

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “We are doing great work, and this is just the beginning. There will be many more good things to come.”

35.speaker: Player
35.text: “Each and every one of you is very capable, but it's what we do as a team that counts.”

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: The ministers weren't as motivated by my statement as I had hoped.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: The ministers looked somewhat motivated by my statement.

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: The ministers appeared energized by my statement.

40.speaker: Lucian Galade
40.text: “Given the current state of the country, improving economic situation is a political priority right now. More so than ever, if we want to win the 58 election.”

52.speaker: Player
52.text: “It's time to hear the opinions on the military.”

67.speaker: Lucian Galade
67.text: “I must also remind you that we promised to focus on security and law enforcement during our campaign.”

68.speaker: Lileas Graf
68.text: “That we are ready to defend our nation, Ms. Walda.”

69.speaker: Ciara Walda
69.text: “Well, here is an argument. The Armed Forces does nothing but eat away financial resources destined for our people while stoking fears for an upcoming *war*.”

70.speaker: Lucian Galade
70.text: “Very worrying. On top of what Paskal said, we need to remember that we promised to focus on healthcare during our election campaign.”

71.speaker: Ciara Walda
71.text: “I agree with Ms. Morgna. We should not reward a structure that is responsible for an ever-increasing number of human rights violations. Additionally, corruption is the reason of our government inefficiencies. It needs to be tackled."

72.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
72.text: “Our healthcare system is vast, and provides free services to most of our citizens. However, the quality of our health services is far worse in low-income and rural areas."

73.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
73.text: “Therefore, I think that we should receive more funding to address this disparity."

74.speaker: Ciara Walda
74.text: “I agree. I have recently begun an investigation into healthcare in Narbel, and the numbers are not good.”

75.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
75.text: “If we don't increase spending on health services, we at least need to maintain it. Otherwise, we are putting lives at risk.”

76.speaker: Ciara Walda
76.text: “Our education system is lacking. Not only in funding but also in modern curricular principles. Our outdated curriculum is wasting our youth.”

77.speaker: Lileas Graf
77.text: “Nonsense. Sordland is still here because of this very system that you insult. How can you insult a system that teaches our sons and daughters the principles of national identity and pride?”

78.speaker: Ciara Walda
78.text: “That is the reason why I advocate two things. An increase of the budget to improve access to education in rural areas, and a new education reform.”

82.speaker: Lucian Galade
82.text: “I must also remind you that we promised that we were going to focus on education during our campaign.”

83.speaker: Iosef Lancea
83.text: “I agree with Lileas. Sordland is Sordland!”

85.speaker: Symon Holl
85.text: “There are three options regarding the budgeting of the four main branches of the government. It's either we increase, maintain or decrease the funding.”

86.speaker: Player
86.text: “Moving away from big government is the right choice.”

87.speaker: Player
87.text: “The problem isn't the amount of money spent. It's how efficiently we spend it.”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “Can we rely on the private sector to support us?”

89.speaker: Symon Holl
89.text: “Increasing will result in an improvement of the branch which will unlock new policy options. Maintaining will keep the funding, resulting in no visible change. Decreasing causes a loss of efficiency in that branch.”

90.speaker: Symon Holl
90.text: “I'm sure we can do that to a certain extent in some branches, like education and health.”

91.speaker: Lucian Galade
91.text: “Sadly, Petr Vectern, Gus Manger and Deivid Wisci won't be attending this meeting.”

94.speaker: Symon Holl
94.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Listened_Education"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Listened_Healthcare"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Listened_LawEnforcement"] == true  or Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Listened_Military"] == true

95.speaker: Symon Holl
95.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Listened_Education"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Listened_Healthcare"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Listened_LawEnforcement"] == true  or Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn03_EnT_Listened_Military"] == true) == false

101.speaker: Symon Holl
101.text: “...The time to make a decision on the budget has come.”

107.speaker: Player
107.text: “Is it possible to maintain as much state control as possible?”

108.speaker: Symon Holl
108.text: “In the health and education departments, yes. However I am not sure if that would be efficient.”

111.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
111.text: “Our welfare systems are full of issues that need to be addressed, for instance."

112.speaker: Ciara Walda
112.text: “It's true that many of our policies could be far better implemented."

113.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
113.text: “We need to be considerate when making such grand choices that have ripple effects.”

114.speaker: Ciara Walda
114.text: “Our universal healthcare system must be protected and not be tainted by private greed or interest.”

115.speaker: Lileas Graf
115.text: “Well, the state provides many services that our citizens pay for with their taxes.”

116.speaker: Ciara Walda
116.text: “I agree. Our essential services should remain under our authority.”

117.speaker: Lucian Galade
117.text: “They are working on the upcoming trade agreements with Wehlen and Agnolia.”

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “I agree with Lileas. If this was another time, I would've said something different but we know the current situation.”

120.speaker: Player
120.text: “I agree with Nia. We need real solutions for real problems like corruption.”

121.speaker: Nia Morgna
121.text: “Directing the funds to my department would solve the problem at its root. If corruption is still rampant, all the police in the world won't help us. We need a specialized Anti-Corruption Police unit which we could create if the funds were directed to me.”

122.speaker: Player
122.text: “I agree with Lucian. We can't just go back on our promise to the people.”

123.speaker: Lileas Graf
123.text: “The police are there to serve and protect the people of Sordland, Ms. Walda and that is exactly what we were doing.”

124.speaker: Lileas Graf
124.text: “More funding will allow us to take care of our police forces. It is quite a simple choice, given the current status of the country.”

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “I agree with Ciara. What would people think of us if we fund the police after all that happened?”

126.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
126.text: “We have just started a new analysis on what would happen if a pandemic struck Sordland. According to the results, if our healthcare facilities remain in their current state, the death toll would be unimaginable.”

127.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
127.text: “This is a matter of life and death, Mr. President and it should be treated as such.”

128.speaker: Player
128.text: “We need to follow through with our promise to the people.”

129.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
129.text: “I'm not even talking about the damage to the economy.”

130.speaker: Player
130.text: “That is indeed worrying. We should try to fix whatever we can as the government.”

132.speaker: Player
132.text: “We need to improve our healthcare. What else are we here for if we can't keep our people alive?”

133.speaker: Iosef Lancea
133.text: “What is there to hear about? I already voiced my opinions.”

134.speaker: Iosef Lancea
134.text: “Rumburg is coming whether we like it or not. If not this year, next year. If not next year, the year after that!”

135.speaker: Iosef Lancea
135.text: “Mr. President. You and I have a shared responsibility to protect this nation from its enemies and I intend to do so until my last breath.”

136.speaker: Iosef Lancea
136.text: “There can be no argument against increasing the budget for our army when there is an enemy on our doorstep, waiting for us to make one wrong move! Anyone who thinks otherwise is a fool!”

137.speaker: Iosef Lancea
137.text: “I will say this with certainty. If Rumburg doesn't make a move against Sordland in 2 or 3 years, my name is not Iosef Lancea!”

139.speaker: Iosef Lancea
139.text: “Right. Pardon my theatrics, sir. But this is a serious matter. The future of our country is up to you, Mr. President.”

140.speaker: Ciara Walda
140.text: “The issues with Rumburg can be solved diplomatically. What kind of a message are we sending to them and the whole world if we suddenly start ramping up our military budget?”

141.speaker: Narrator
141.text: Iosef was beginning to lose control of the volume of his voice.

143.speaker: Player
143.text: “People elected us for a reason. We will answer their needs.”

144.speaker: Player
144.text: “I agree with Iosef. Rumburg is a real threat and we need to be ready.”

145.speaker: Player
145.text: “I agree with Ciara. We need to be as diplomatic as possible.”

146.speaker: Player
146.text: “There are other more important avenues that our money can be better spent on.”

147.speaker: Ciara Walda
147.text: “We need to ensure the new generation is as well educated as their counterparts in more modern countries.”

148.speaker: Ciara Walda
148.text: “To be honest, Sordland is lacking compared to Arcasia and United Contana when it comes to education levels. The backbone of any country is its people, and we need to protect our future.”

149.speaker: Lileas Graf
149.text: “We won't be compared to other countries. Sordland is Sordland.”

150.speaker: Player
150.text: “You are right Lucian. We can't let people down.”

151.speaker: Player
151.text: “Lileas is right. We will pave our own path. We didn't get this far by imitating Arcasia or United Contana.”

152.speaker: Player
152.text: “I agree with Ciara. It is high time we invest in education and enact reforms.”

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: Symon placed a stack of papers on my table.

159.speaker: Symon Holl
159.text: “As we manage the government budget, we can to go into debt to invest in different branches.”

160.speaker: Symon Holl
160.text: “Before we begin our discussion, there is one more thing that I want to voice my opinion on.”

161.speaker: Symon Holl
161.text: “This budget will also be applicable to our entire term. It is very critical that we plan correctly.”

171.speaker: Ciara Walda
171.text: “Before we begin, is nobody going to mention the ban on the Red Youth?”

172.speaker: Nia Morgna
172.text: “Before we begin, is nobody going to mention the ban on the Young Sords?"

173.speaker: Lileas Graf
173.text: “Did you just roll your eyes at me, young lady?”
173.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanRedYouth"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanYoungSords"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanBoth"] == true) == false)

174.speaker: Nia Morgna
174.text: "However much their political aims might differ from our administration's, surely you must agree that freedom of expression must be protected at all costs."

175.speaker: Nia Morgna
175.text: "However much their political aims might differ from our administration's, surely you must agree that freedom of expression must be protected at all costs."

176.speaker: Ciara Walda
176.text: “*If* I did, it's because religion has no place at a government budget meeting."

177.speaker: Player
177.text: “Please leave your religion at the Maroon Palace gates, Ms. Graf."

178.speaker: Player
178.text: “If you have problems with the ban, call a separate meeting with me."

179.speaker: Player
179.text: "The ban is final. Don't question it any further."

180.speaker: Ciara Walda
180.text: "Yes, and may I just add that--"

181.speaker: Ciara Walda
181.text: "Nia-- I mean, Ms. Morgna -- is right."

182.speaker: Lileas Graf
182.text: “I was merely expressing my wishes for a successful trade deal. Freedom of expression must be protected at all costs, must it not, Ms. Morgna?"

183.speaker: Narrator
183.text: Ciara gave a barely disguised eye roll.

184.speaker: Narrator
184.text: Nia flashed her an appreciative smile.

185.speaker: Nia Morgna
185.text: “Thank you for bringing that up, Cia-- Ms. Walda. I agree that however much the Red Youth's political aims might differ from our administration's, freedom of expression must be protected at all costs."

186.speaker: Narrator
186.text: She broke off as she noticed that Lucian, Symon and Iosef were looking at her and Nia in stony silence.

187.speaker: Lucian Galade
187.text: "Ladies. Let's leave the extraneous chit-chat for afternoon tea."

188.speaker: Narrator
188.text: Ciara shot a pleading look at Lileas, who merely pursed her lips disapprovingly.

189.speaker: Narrator
189.text: Nia flashed her an appreciative smile.

190.speaker: Ciara Walda
190.text: "I myself strongly disagree with the Young Sords' politics, but even I believe that--"

191.speaker: Nia Morgna
191.text: “Before we begin, is nobody going to mention the ban on the Red Youth and Young Sords?"
191.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanRedYouth"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanYoungSords"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanBoth"] == true)

192.speaker: Ciara Walda
192.text: "Nia-- I mean, Ms. Morgna -- is right."

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: Nia flashed her an appreciative smile.

194.speaker: Ciara Walda
194.text: "I myself align far closer to the Red Youth's politics than the Young Sords' but I believe that both--"

195.speaker: Nia Morgna
195.text: "Actually, in this case I agree with Cia-- Ms. Walda."

196.speaker: Narrator
196.text: Ciara flashed her an appreciative smile.

197.speaker: Nia Morgna
197.text: "According to Sordland's laws regarding the separation of Sanctuary and state--"

198.speaker: Narrator
198.text: She broke off as she noticed that Symon, Lucian and Iosef were looking at the three female ministers in stony silence.

199.speaker: Lucian Galade
199.text: "Ladies. Let's leave the extraneous chit-chat for afternoon tea."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "The Lord is always welcome in these halls, Ms. Walda."

201.speaker: Narrator
201.text: Symon started loudly shuffling some documents around. All eyes turned to the Minister of Economy.

203.speaker: Narrator
203.text: Lileas was about to utter a word but a loud cough from Symon interrupted the silence in the room.

205.speaker: Player
205.text: “We should spend as much as possible to achieve growth.”

206.speaker: Player
206.text: “Our administration should be fiscally conservative to avoid a crash.”

207.speaker: Lucian Galade
207.text: “A stimulating strategy could have positive political effects with increased support.”

208.speaker: Lucian Galade
208.text: “Measures of austerity have shown difficulties in appeasing voter groups.”

211.speaker: Player
211.text: “I have made up my mind about the budget. We can proceed.”
